question: Will H.R. 33 (United States–Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act) be enacted into law before May 1, 2026?
summary: Senate action risk remains strong: no final Senate passage or presidential signature by May 1, 2026.
House passage in January 2025 shows momentum, but it does not guarantee Senate approval or enactment.
Historical enactment rates for introduced federal bills are very low, supporting downward pressure on the likelihood.
Ongoing Treasury negotiations toward a broader U.S.–Taiwan tax framework provide some upside potential, though not a guarantee of enactment.

justification.critique_assessment: Yes, objections valid and highlight meaningful downward pressure (Senate inaction and low historical rates) while acknowledging some upside from House momentum and negotiations.
justification.adjustment: Lowered the probability from 0.04 to 0.03 to reflect stronger downward risks; set range 0.02–0.06 to capture remaining uncertainty.

forecasts.reference-class: General probability that a randomly introduced federal bill becomes law in the U.S. Congress (across topics, environments, and time periods).

sources.claim: Metaculus forecast assigns a 25% probability of H.R.33 being enacted into law before May 1, 2026.

H.R.33 was introduced on January 3, 2025 and, as of January 16, 2025, had been received in the Senate and referred to the Committee on Finance; the House passed the bill with a 423-1 vote on January 15-16, 2025.
House passage of H.R.33 occurred January 15, 2025 by a 423-1 vote.
Senate companion bill S.199 to H.R.33 was introduced January 23, 2025.
S.199, the Senate companion to H.R.33, was introduced in the Senate on January 23, 2025.
Taipei Times reports U.S. House passed H.R.33 in January 2025; no evidence of final enactment by May 1, 2026.
Academic base rate: among roughly 70,000 bills introduced (2001–2015), about 2,513 were enacted (approximately 3.6%).
Senate status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance (as of Jan 16, 2025).
Finance, Foreign Relations Committees introduced companion U.S.-Taiwan tax legislation to H.R. 33.
U.S. House of Representatives passed the United States–Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act by 423-1 (January 15, 2025).
Neal Statement on House Passage of H.R. 33 describing House approval and urging Senate action.
Treasury: U.S. and Taiwan to begin negotiating a comprehensive tax agreement addressing double taxation.
June 4, 2025 bipartisan letter urging Senate to promptly take up the U.S.–Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act.
All Info page confirms status (introduced Jan 3, 2025; Senate action ongoing; not yet enacted).
H.R.33 status shows the Senate received the bill on January 16, 2025 and referred to the Senate Finance Committee after the House passed the bill on January 15, 2025.
Text indicates provisions for United States-Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act and notes that the bill passed the House (January 15, 2025).
Ways and Means press release announcing the House action approving H.R.33 on January 16, 2025.
Senate committees introduced a companion U.S.-Taiwan tax-legislation bill in January 2025 as a companion to H.R.33.
Axios summarizes that the 118th Congress passed the fewest laws in decades, highlighting a historically low enactment rate for federal legislation.
Taipei Times reports that the U.S. House passed the United States-Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act by a 423-1 vote.

causal-factors.name: Senate enactment path uncertain / Senate inaction as of 2026-03-01
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 1, 2026 there is no final Senate passage or presidential signature for H.R.33; the bill cleared the House in January 2025 and a Senate companion was introduced, but enshrinement into law by May 1, 2026 remains uncertain. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/33/text?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: House passage indicates strong initial momentum
causal-factors.rationale: The U.S. House passed H.R.33 in January 2025 by a wide margin (423-1), signaling strong bipartisan support and momentum. ([waysandmeans.house.gov](https://waysandmeans.house.gov/2025/01/16/house-approves-fairer-tax-treatment-for-american-workers-and-manufacturers-strengthening-competitive-edge-against-china/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Senate companion introduced indicates momentum to act in both chambers
causal-factors.rationale: A Senate companion (S.199) was introduced January 23, 2025, reflecting ongoing bicameral momentum, though not yet enacted. ([foreign.senate.gov](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/press/dem/release/finance-foreign-relations-committees-introduce-us-taiwan-tax-legislation?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate for enacted federal bills is very low
causal-factors.rationale: Academic and public-utility assessments show a small fraction of introduced bills become law; typical enactment rates are in the single-digit percentages. ([guides.brooklaw.edu](https://guides.brooklaw.edu/federal_legislative_history_research/legislative_process?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Ongoing Treasury negotiations could influence path but do not guarantee enactment
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury announced negotiations toward a comprehensive U.S.–Taiwan tax agreement, which could shape the tax-relief framework but does not ensure passage of H.R.33 itself. ([home.treasury.gov](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2693?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Prediction-market anchor (Metaculus) cited at 25% likelihood
causal-factors.rationale: Metaculus forecasts list a 25% probability, which is relatively optimistic given the current Senate status and historical enactment rates; the actual path appears more constrained. ([metaculus.com](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/42246/will-hr-33-united-statestaiwan-expedited-double-tax-relief-act-be-enacted-into-law-before-may-1/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Senate action risk (no final enactment by 2026-05-01)
causal-factors.rationale: Senate has only received S.199 (introduced Jan 23, 2025) and has not enacted a companion into law as of May 1, 2026; without Senate passage and presidential signature, enactment cannot occur.

causal-factors.name: House passage with bipartisan support
causal-factors.rationale: H.R. 33 passed the House with a 423-1 vote in January 2025, signaling strong congressional support that could translate into Senate action.

causal-factors.name: Ongoing US-Taiwan tax-negotiation framework
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury and the Administration signaled willingness to negotiate a comprehensive tax agreement; progress toward an agreement could enable implementing legislation and final enactment.

causal-factors.name: Historical low enactment rate for introduced bills
causal-factors.rationale: Academic and recent historical data show a very small share of introduced bills become law (roughly 3.6% in 2001–2015), and the 118th Congress was notably unproductive.

causal-factors.name: Requirement for both approval and implementing legislation tied to a negotiated agreement
causal-factors.rationale: Enactment would require not only approval but also implementing legislation and a binding tax agreement, adding multiple legislative hurdles.

causal-factors.name: Election-year and budget/legislative priorities in 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Political dynamics in 2026 could either slow or accelerate action, but the effect is uncertain and context-dependent.

causal-factors.name: Senate action status and timetable
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 1, 2026 there is no public record of Senate passage or presidential signature for H.R. 33, and the bill remains without enacted status despite a Senate referral in 2025.

causal-factors.name: House momentum and bicameral alignment
causal-factors.rationale: H.R. 33 passed the House with broad bipartisan support (423-1) in January 2025, signaling strong legislative momentum if the Senate acts.

causal-factors.name: Senate companion progress
causal-factors.rationale: A Senate companion (S.199) was introduced in January 2025 and Senate committees have engaged, indicating cross-chamber attention that could raise enactment chances.

causal-factors.name: Treasury negotiations on a comprehensive U.S.–Taiwan tax agreement
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury announced in 2024 that negotiations to address double taxation would begin; progress toward a negotiated framework could spur implementing legislation and raise the likelihood of final action.

causal-factors.name: Election-year dynamics and competing legislative priorities
causal-factors.rationale: The 2026 election cycle tends to elevate gridlock and crowd out ancillary tax-relief bills unless they become top-tier priorities.

synthesis: The ensemble implies a low likelihood of enactment by May 1, 2026. Given strong downward risks from Senate inaction and historical passage rates, a modest downward adjustment is warranted, though House momentum and ongoing negotiations keep a nonzero chance alive.
